filters.organism: Homo sapiens for the human sweep; unrestricted for the viral and bacterial sweeps

primary_frame.note: A depositor's own use of the word 'allosteric' is a claim, not curation. This frame is a RECALL device only. Clause (ii) decides, from primary literature, per target. See docs/benchmark/secondary/evidence/databases.md for why no curated allostery database can serve as the frame.

secondary_frame.note: Domain-by-domain sweeps of the allosteric-enzymology and allosteric-drug literature, run to reach families the full-text frame misses -- classical effectors such as AMP and UMP are rarely described with the word 'allosteric' in a PDB title. Disclosed as a second recall device, subject to the same clause (ii) test.

candidates.name: acly
candidates.detail: NDI-091143 is competitive versus citrate (Ki 7.0 +/- 0.8 nM), so its effect on citrate turnover is direct competition. 6POE is also a CoA complex, not a matched apo. Re-examined 2026-08-24 against the retrieved IUPHAR XC text, which allows a bitopic ligand to occupy both sites and still behave competitively: the competition argument alone no longer decides. The rejection stands on the second ground, the unmatched apo.

candidates.name: usp7
candidates.detail: GNE-6640 competes with ubiquitin, a natural binding partner. Partner competition is not allostery. Re-examined 2026-08-24: this is a REPOSITORY reading, not IUPHAR's. IUPHAR XC section III asks only that the properties of one ligand be altered by a second ligand at a nonoverlapping, topographically distinct site, and it allows competitive behaviour via bitopic engagement. This rejection therefore rests on a principle this repo asserted rather than on a cited threshold, and it is the one clause (ii) decision the corrected reading puts in doubt. Not reopened: re-admitting an arm changes N and reruns the seeded tier split, which is a re-freeze.
